\chapter{María, España --- The Nouns That Need No Article}
\label{ch:nombres-propios}
\hlchaptermodality{260}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use names and titles with the right article, or none.}

I can use names and titles with the right article, or none.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[María · España · profesor]{María · España · profesor — the nouns that need no article}

\label{lesson:ES-C66-nombres-propios}



\begin{quote}
\emph{El libro}, \emph{la casa}. The article's job is to say \textbf{which one}.

Now try putting one in front of a person's name and hear how wrong it sounds.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: nothing left for the article to do}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{Veo a} \emph{\textbf{María}}. — not \emph{a la María}. \emph{Vivo en} \emph{\textbf{España}}. — not \emph{en la España}.
\end{quote}

A \textbf{proper noun} — a name, a country, a city — already points at exactly one thing in the world. The article exists to narrow a noun down to one, and here there is nothing left to narrow. So it goes.

That is the rule you have been following since the first time you said \emph{Me llamo…}, and it has never been stated.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
Now the part that catches people, and it follows from the same logic.

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{Hablo con} \emph{\textbf{el profesor}} \emph{García.} & talking \textbf{about} him — article \\
\emph{\textbf{Profesor}} \emph{García, ¿puedo hablar?} & talking \textbf{to} him — none \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

A title is not a name. \emph{Profesor} is an ordinary noun, so it takes an article like any other — until you turn and address the person, at which point you are not identifying them for anybody. You are calling them. And a vocative takes no article, exactly as it takes no personal \emph{a}.

Same rule underneath: the article says which one, and it appears precisely when that job needs doing.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Veo a María}, \emph{Vivo en España}
  \item \emph{el profesor García}, then \emph{Profesor García, …}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Why do names take no article? (They already point at \textbf{one} thing.)

And when does a title lose its article? (When you are \textbf{addressing} the person.)
\end{tcolorbox}
